papers.title_en: Geometry-Preserving in 3D Gaussian Splatting for LiDAR-Camera Extrinsic Calibration
papers.authors: Kyoleen Kwak, Daeho Kim, Jeong Woon Lee, Hyoseok Hwang
papers.evidence: 激光雷达-相机外参标定用于多模态感知
papers.tldr: 针对现有基于3D高斯泼溅的标定方法偏重渲染质量导致代理几何偏离真实LiDAR结构的问题，提出一种几何保持框架，在可微分优化中施加LiDAR点云几何约束，实现精确的LiDAR-相机外参标定。实验表明该方法能有效保持几何一致性，为稳健的多模态感知提供可靠校准。该工作提升了LiDAR与相机之间的跨模态对齐精度，对自动驾驶等场景中的融合感知至关重要。
papers.abstract_en: Accurate LiDAR-camera calibration is essential for robust multi-modal perception. Targetless approaches avoid manual setup but remain limited by the scarcity of discriminative cross-modal features. Recent methods address this by reconstructing the scene within a differentiable model, enabling extrinsic optimization through dense photometric supervision. Among these, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has been widely adopted as a geometric proxy that bridges LiDAR and camera within a single differentiable framework. However, since 3DGS was originally designed for novel view synthesis, existing methods tend to prioritize rendering quality, causing the proxy geometry to drift from the true LiDAR structure. We propose a framework that preserves the metric geometry of the Gaussian proxy by aggregating multi-view LiDAR observations for dense depth supervision and blocking photometric gradients from updating the Gaussian spatial parameters. We validate our method on public driving datasets, where it consistently outperforms existing targetless methods in calibration accuracy.

papers.title_en: Aerial-ground LiDAR place recognition with patch-level self-supervised learning and expanded reciprocal re-ranking
papers.authors: Yandi Yang, Xianghong Zou, Jianping Li, Haofeng Xie, Saurav Uprety, Hongzhou Yang, Naser El-Sheimy
papers.evidence: 使用空地和地面激光雷达点云进行跨视角地点识别
papers.tldr: 地面LiDAR地点识别受限于预访需求和覆盖不全，而利用空中激光扫描（ALS）地图可克服此问题，但面临域间隙和初始检索误报挑战。为此，提出一种新颖的检索与重排序框架：检索网络通过多尺度块级自监督学习增强空地点云全局特征判别力，并设计扩展互惠（ER）重排序算法利用邻域信息精炼特征。在CS-Urban-Scenes上，平均Recall@1提升9.8%，ER重排序再提升10.2%，且在CS-Campus3D上也取得最佳性能，显著提升了空对地地点识别的精度与鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: LiDAR place recognition determines one's position on a prior point cloud map. The most studied ground-level LiDAR place recognition suffers from pre-visit requirements, incomplete coverage, and limited perspectives. Using pre-acquired, full-coverage Airborne Laser Scanning (ALS) data as an aerial prior map overcomes these drawbacks, making cross-view place recognition necessary and advantageous. However, aerial-ground LiDAR place recognition faces significant challenges, including the domain gap between aerial and ground point clouds, and false positives during initial retrieval. To address these challenges, we present a novel retrieval and re-ranking framework for aerial-ground LiDAR place recognition. Based on the priors that neighboring point cloud patches share similar semantics with anchor patch, our retrieval network introduces patch-level self-supervised learning modules at multiple scales and integrates with scene-level learning to improve global feature discriminativeness between aerial and ground point clouds. Furthermore, leveraging the structured spatial distribution of ALS point clouds, we introduce an Expanded Reciprocal (ER) re-ranking algorithm to exploit neighborhood information maximally and refine each feature based on neighbor features, which are then used to update the similarity matrix for final ranking. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our retrieval network outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, achieving a 9.8\% improvement in average Recall@1 and a 3.2\% improvement in average Recall@1\% on the CS-Urban-Scenes, while also showing the best performance on the CS-Campus3D dataset. Additionally, our ER re-ranking algorithm further boosts the average Recall@1 by 4.9\% on CS-Campus3D and 10.2\% on CS-Urban-Scenes without additional training.

papers.title_en: Monocular 3D Occupancy Perception for Robots on Sidewalks via Hybrid 2D-3D Learning
papers.authors: Yukai Ma, Joe Lin, Liu Liu, Honglin He, Lulu Ricketts, Brad Squicciarini, Yong Liu, Bolei Zhou
papers.evidence: 结合LiDAR-RGB配对数据与单目学习进行3D占用感知
papers.tldr: 人行道场景杂乱无结构，现有3D占用学习方法依赖大规模配对LiDAR-RGB数据，成本高且难以迁移。提出WalkOCC框架，利用少量配对数据生成伪占用监督，再联合大量无配对单目图像进行混合2D-3D学习，实现稳定优化与泛化。在引入的Sidewalk3D数据集上，模型预测精度一致提升，能精细分割路缘、排水沟等细微结构，并对环境变化和不同机器人平台表现出鲁棒性。该方法降低了昂贵3D标注依赖，为人行道机器人安全导航提供了高效可扩展的感知方案。
papers.abstract_en: Sidewalks in the real world are crowded, cluttered, and less structured than roads, making 3D occupancy prediction a key ingredient for the safe navigation of mobile robots such as delivery bots and electric wheelchairs. Existing occupancy learning pipelines are largely designed for on-road autonomous driving and often train on large-scale paired LiDAR-RGB datasets with dense 3D supervision and multiple camera inputs, which are costly to collect and do not adequately capture sidewalk-specific characteristics. We propose WalkOCC, a hybrid Ray-marching monocular 3D occupancy perception framework for robots operating on sidewalks. WalkOCC explicitly couples geometric grounding from LiDAR-RGB paired data with scalable learning from large-scale unpaired monocular images. It bootstraps pseudo occupancy supervision from paired sequences and jointly learns image-level representations on additional 2D-only data. It yields stable optimization and improved generalization without requiring costly 3D occupancy annotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent gains in prediction accuracy, fine-grained segmentation of subtle urban structures such as curbs and gutters, and robustness to environmental and cross-embodiment shifts compared with self-supervised image-based baselines. To facilitate evaluation and benchmarking, we also introduce Sidewalk3D, a large-scale sidewalk perception dataset with LiDAR-camera paired sequences collected across multiple locations and time periods, along with 3D semantic occupancy annotations for evaluation. Code and data will be made available.

papers.title_en: LIT-GS: LiDAR-Inertial-Thermal Gaussian Splatting for Illumination-Robust Mapping
papers.authors: Shikuan Shi, Chunran Zheng, Jiaming Xu, Tianyong Ye, Tao Yu, Yukang Cui
papers.evidence: 激光雷达-惯性-热成像多模态融合用于鲁棒建图
papers.tldr: 现有LiDAR-惯性-视觉高斯映射依赖RGB光度线索，在光照突变和弱纹理场景中易失效。LIT-GS融合热成像与LiDAR平面几何约束，利用视觉地图点作为置信度跨模态锚点，通过加权点面残差联合优化位姿与三维点，并引入平面正则化可微分 Splatting 目标抑制表面厚化和结构漂移。实验表明该方法在挑战性光照下显著提升几何精度与渲染质量，为光照鲁棒实时神经渲染开辟新途径。
papers.abstract_en: Gaussian Splatting has enabled real-time neural rendering, yet existing LiDAR-inertial-visual (LIV) Gaussian mapping pipelines remain fragile under illumination changes and texture-deficient scenes due to their reliance on RGB photometric cues. We present LIT-GS, a LiDAR-inertial-thermal Gaussian Splatting framework that injects LiDAR-derived plane geometry as an explicit constraint in both pose/structure refinement and Gaussian optimization. Specifically, we exploit LIV visual map points as confidence-aware cross-modal anchors to establish reliable thermal-LiDAR associations, and incorporate weighted LiDAR point-to-plane residuals into bundle adjustment to jointly refine camera poses and 3D points under weak thermal supervision. Building on the refined structure, we further introduce a LiDAR-plane-regularized differentiable splatting objective that constrains rendered 3D points to align with locally observed planes, mitigating surface thickening and structural drift in low-contrast thermal imagery. Experiments on proprietary sequences and public datasets demonstrate that LIT-GS consistently improves geometric accuracy and rendering quality over state-of-the-art LIV-based Gaussian Splatting baselines, particularly in challenging lighting conditions.

papers.title_en: Point Cloud Upsampling through Patch-based Frequency Superposition
papers.authors: Marina Ritthaler, Azhar Hussian, Vasileios Belagiannis, André Kaup
papers.evidence: 基于频率叠加的优化驱动点云上采样
papers.tldr: 针对现有深度学习点云上采样方法缺乏可解释性且依赖训练数据的缺点，提出PUtPFS，一种基于补丁频率叠加的优化方法，通过选择稀疏区域和叠加空间频率估计曲面来生成新点，实现均匀上采样。实验表明该方法无需训练即可在不同数据集上表现优异，为稀疏LiDAR点云生成稠密数据提供了高效方案。
papers.abstract_en: In recent years, neural networks have become the dominant models in most point cloud upsampling methods. Although these approaches are achieving good results, they do have drawbacks, such as a lack of interpretability and data dependency. Moreover, they have to be trained on a dataset that is similar to the test data in order to perform well. To avoid these disadvantages, we propose Point Cloud Upsampling through Patch-based Frequency Superposition (PUtPFS), an optimization-based approach that selects subsets of points and estimates the surface of this set through superpositioning spatial frequencies. Then, new points are placed on this surface. By successively selecting points in the least dense regions of the point cloud, a uniform upsampling can be reached. With this method, we surpass the current best upsampling results in the commonly considered point-to-surface distance. Furthermore, we achieve the best Chamfer and Hausdorff distance among the optimization-based approaches. As an additional advantage, our method does not need any training data and is mathematically interpretable.
